allowed_claims: EU isolation is enabled by default for every Fathom customer; there is nothing to set up.
No setup, tweaking, or changes to the embed script are required to use EU isolation.

EU isolation also covers visitors from the non-EU-member nations Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
Fathom's EU servers are located in Falkenstein, Helsinki, and Nuremberg.
Customers who need all global traffic routed through the EU (Extreme EU Isolation) can use the script URL https://cdn-eu.usefathom.com/script.js instead of the default embed script.
Firewall settings are adjusted by going to Settings, then Sites, clicking on the site, then clicking the Firewall tab.
The firewall offers separate list tabs for Pages, IPs, Referrers, Domains, Countries, and Events.

Blocking pages, IPs, domains, or countries in the firewall does not prevent visitors from accessing or navigating the site; it only prevents their visits from being shown as data in the Fathom dashboard.
Currently, only IPv4 addresses are supported for wildcard IP blocking in the firewall.
Once one or more allowed domains are added to the firewall's Domains list, data from any other domain is blocked instantly.

In the Events firewall tab, Block drops the specified event names while still collecting every other event, Allow collects only the listed names and wildcard patterns, and an empty allow list collects every event.
The firewall only stops future visits; existing spam already recorded in reports must be removed separately using Data removals in the site's Manage settings.
An empty firewall list does not filter any traffic.
Fathom's tracking script can be installed via a WordPress plugin or one of Fathom's other integrations.
Fathom's dashboard is live and real-time, so installation can be verified by checking whether a visit appears in the Realtime count at the top of the dashboard.
Once allowed domains are set in the site firewall settings, Fathom filters out data from any hostname not on that list, including local, staging, and test domains.

IP address filtering to exclude staging/local visits works well for a single developer or a small, stable set of IP addresses, whereas allowed domains are more reliable for teams and changing networks.
Fathom provides a browser console command, fathom.blockTrackingForMe();, run on a page where Fathom is installed, to block tracking in the current browser.
The browser-console tracking block set via fathom.blockTrackingForMe() is stored in the browser's local storage, so it keeps working for future visits from that browser.
Fathom shows analytics in real time, so a working exclusion means a non-live visit should not appear as a current visitor on the dashboard.
Starting to use Fathom Analytics requires adding a single line of code to the header section of the website, containing the site's actual Site ID.
Fathom's site firewall settings support blocking pages, blocking IPs, blocking countries, and blocking domains.
Fathom's advanced script settings support ignoring canonicals, honouring Do Not Track (DNT), and single-page applications (SPAs), among other options.
Each Fathom site has a unique Site ID that is required for the tracking snippet, integrations, and API calls.
EU visitors' personal data stays in the EU, while anonymized analytics are stored on Fathom's US infrastructure.
Fathom's Data Isolation feature is included for all customers on all plans and requires no programming or setup.
Using Fathom means no cookie notices are required.

Fathom Analytics counts Bootstrap, IBM, HashiCorp, GitHub, The New York Times and Laravel among the companies using it.
Fathom does not charge extra for historical GA4 imports.

Fathom's GA4 importer brings in supported daily analytics available through Google's API, but does not recreate every GA4 report or import GA events.

Large GA4 imports may need to be split into smaller date ranges.

Currently, only IPv4 addresses are supported for wildcard IP blocking in the firewall.
Once one or more allowed domains are added to the firewall's Domains list, data from any other domain is blocked instantly.

In the Events firewall tab, Block drops the specified event names while still collecting every other event, Allow collects only the listed names and wildcard patterns, and an empty allow list collects every event.
